Launch Open Audience campaign on 5 hoodies at Rs.1,000/day. |DETAILS| Instruction: Start a new open audience video campaign for ages 18-65, India-wide with no exclusions, at Rs.1,000/day with 5 ads — HD001 Black Legacy Hoodie (Rs.1999), HD003 Off White Blue Flames Hoodie (Rs.2199), HD002 Black Voilet Thunder Hoodie (Rs.1999), HD004 Off White God Child Hoodie (Rs.2199), HD007 Red Blessed Hoodie (Rs.2199). No ROAS floor. The campaign goes live as built. Reasoning: The account has never spent: get_seller_account_age returns no weekly rows, get_meta_campaign_settings returns no campaigns, get_seller_active_adsets returns no active ad sets. Rs.1,000/day is the standard first-campaign budget and is the account's whole envelope (get_seller_target_vs_current_budget returns no row, so there is no configured target budget on file). Ad account 1604996531360413 confirmed from get_seller_config_build, the only source for a seller who has never run an ad. Open Audience chosen because a lookalike needs a seed and the account has 2 lifetime orders; get_campaign_routing_recommendation returned no route for this seller, so the route is NOT CHECKED and the type is chosen from seed-size evidence instead. All five products verified active, visible and in stock at 179-180 units each (get_inventory_check) with selling prices and costs confirmed in get_seller_catalogue. No roas_floor set, so the campaign bids LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP: the pixel has recorded essentially nothing and a floor derived from the 13.17% category benchmark asks Meta to clear a return this seller has never achieved, which would starve delivery at launch. Each ad carries its own video, so the account learns which of the five hoodies converts. DEVIATION from the work order: the work order specified both age 18-65 and men-only, but a new campaign can narrow on age OR gender, not both. Age was kept and the gender restriction dropped, because a men's-hoodie catalogue on a wide age band still lands on men, while dropping the age band would leave the campaign on an unspecified age range with no read at all. Watch the age split in the first-week read and narrow to men as a targeting change once there is data. RTO tripwire is set at 55% rather than the 45.70% category benchmark because the seller's own two lifetime orders are both COD and both still sitting in post-purchase hold with zero delivered and zero attempted (get_logistics_partner_data, get_fad_by_segment), and both read 100% RTO on sr delhivery surface at Rs.129 forward logistics per order against a Rs.80.88/AWB benchmark - the account's real RTO exposure may exceed the benchmark, so the tripwire is deliberately set at the worse reading., Ask seller to republish hidden catalogue products and approve a coupon ladder. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller whether the stocked but hidden catalogue products should be republished on the storefront (about 30 products are active with 30-60 units in stock each but are not visible), and ask seller to approve a coupon ladder against the account AOV of Rs.2,099 - bands near Rs.4,199 and Rs.6,299 - to be set up once the cost conversation has landed. Reasoning: The catalogue gap is real: get_seller_catalogue returns 8 live visible in-stock products and get_seller_catalogue_quality_summary confirms live_products 8, while get_inventory_check shows roughly 30 further products with is_active=True and stock of 30-60 units each that do not appear in the catalogue read, meaning they are not visible or are flagged OOS. Their per-product is_visible and is_oos flags were NOT CHECKED, so this is a question for the seller rather than an assumption about which are launchable. The coupon gap is measured: get_seller_website_checkout_config returns active_generic_coupon_count 0 and active_generic_coupons empty against aov_for_coupon_check of Rs.2,099, so a healthy ladder wants bands near Rs.4,199 and Rs.6,299. Both are deliberately deferred rather than actioned, because the COGS gap is upstream of both - a discount coupon against a 55% COGS product spends the thinnest part of the margin stack, and at a 25% price cut contribution per order would already be down to Rs.144-168. No catalogue, price, coupon or budget change is being made now, so this action carries no side effect on the running campaign., Confirm the 2 lifetime orders have shipped before scaling spend. |DETAILS| Instruction: Confirm the seller's two existing orders have shipped and left post-purchase hold, and that delivery is being attempted, before any spend above Rs.1,000/day on the launch campaign. Reasoning: Added because the seller's own order history is a risk the strategy report did not surface. get_logistics_partner_data shows both lifetime orders (2 total, 100% of orders) sitting in post-purchase hold with awb_nc 2, delivered 0, in_transit 0, pph 2, on courier 'sr delhivery surface' with zero first-attempt delivery. get_fad_by_segment confirms attempted 0, first_attempt_delivered 0, not_yet_attempted 0 for the window 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-28. get_logistics_partner_payment_mode_data shows both orders on COD with rto_prec 100 and logistics_forward_spend Rs.129 per order against a Rs.80.88/AWB category benchmark. The storefront promises a 6-day delivery (display_delivery_date_non_customised_max_day 6), so an order sitting in PPH is already outside the promise shown to buyers. This is a check, not a diagnosis: the orders are recent and the 2-order sample is far below the 10 non-cancelled orders needed to read an RTO rate in either direction, so the correct response is to verify dispatch works before scaling, not to call an RTO problem. The launch itself is not blocked - Rs.1,000/day is the account's whole envelope and the campaign's job is to buy learning - but no spend above that should go in while dispatch is unproven, because COD orders from a seller whose shipments are stuck would convert learning spend into RTO and return shipping., Hold launch-set prices at Rs.1,999 / Rs.2,199 - no price change. |DETAILS| Instruction: Do not change the selling price on HD001 (Rs.1,999), HD002 (Rs.1,999), HD003 (Rs.2,199), HD004 (Rs.2,199) or HD007 (Rs.2,199). Leave all five prices exactly as they are on the storefront until the cost conversation is settled. Reasoning: Recorded so the next person does not 'fix' this. Verified current state: get_seller_catalogue and get_inventory_check agree on all five prices (HD001 Rs.1999, HD002 Rs.1999, HD003 Rs.2199, HD004 Rs.2199, HD007 Rs.2199) and on costs (HD001/HD002 Rs.1100, HD003-HD008 Rs.1200). Commission is 3.54% (get_product_level_data_with_marketplace and get_platform_level_data); category benchmark RTO is 45.70% and logistics Rs.80.88/AWB (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking); category S/GMV is 13.17%. The seller's own breakeven is unavailable - get_seller_breakeven_sgmv and get_breakeven_sgmv both return no row. Arithmetic in python_sandbox on the tools' own profit formula (profit_perc = 100 - new_cogs - L%NMV - M%NMV - commission), the strategy stage's headline break-even figures of 4.8% at current prices and 24.5% at a 25% cut could not be reproduced: the 4.8% is the sign-flipped magnitude of the shipped-COGS figure (a negative headroom reported as positive), while the 24.5% comes from the delivered-COGS basis, so the two figures came from inconsistent bases. Recomputed on both bases, break-even S/GMV at current prices is -4.8%/20.3% (HD001) and -4.2%/20.7% (HD003), and at a 25% cut it is -23.9%/9.6% and -23.1%/10.2%. The conclusion the strategy reached is still right, but for a stronger reason: a lower break-even percentage is not more margin. Contribution per order net of commission and logistics falls from Rs.406 to Rs.144 on HD001 and Rs.456 to Rs.168 on HD003 if price is cut 25%, so every order would land but none would be worth much - gross profit per order falls from Rs.899 to Rs.399 (HD001) and Rs.999 to Rs.449 (HD003), and COGS rises from 55.0% to 73.4%. The seller's price is genuinely above the market (Shopdeck comparables at Rs.539-Rs.999 and marketplace listings at Rs.474-Rs.1,549), so the gap is real; the cost structure, not the price, is the binding constraint. No update_selling_price action is issued for any of the five products, exactly as the work order specifies., Ask seller to cut hoodie cost to Rs.900 / Rs.960. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller to reduce hoodie cost from Rs.1,100 (HD001 Black Legacy Hoodie, HD002 Black Voilet Thunder Hoodie) and Rs.1,200 (HD003, HD004, HD007) toward about Rs.900 and Rs.960. The category benchmark is 43.60% (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking, mens-clothing) - an 11.4pp gap. fetch_hygiene_actions independently flags all 32 visible SKUs as 'Update all visible SKUs to have cogs less than 50%', so the standard is confirmed from two directions. The arithmetic in python_sandbox shows why this gates the price decision: at cost Rs.900/Rs.960 the launch set holds COGS of 45.0% and 43.7% - at or below the category benchmark - which is what makes a later price of Rs.1,499-Rs.1,649 affordable at roughly 58-60% COGS, whereas at today's cost that price would run at 72.8-73.4% COGS and cut contribution per order from Rs.406-456 to Rs.144-168. This is a sourcing conversation and cannot be executed by the operator, so it is recorded as a seller ask with no action_type; it must not be converted into a price change. A 10-20% cost improvement is hard but plausible at this scale., Ask seller for UGC video on HD001 and HD003 product pages. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller to supply a UGC video for HD001 Black Legacy Hoodie (zcImU3UWYTKQ) and HD003 Off White Blue Flames Hoodie (Dvot12IIdZVe), and add it to both product pages before the launch campaign carries meaningful spend. Product links resolve to https://sspbanoras.com/catalogue/<product_id>/0, built from custom_domain in get_seller_website_checkout_config., Ask seller to cut sourcing cost 10-15% on the launch sarees. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to negotiate a 10-15% lower cost price on the four launch sarees (catlog-f3, catlog-f1, catlog-f8, catlog-f5), from Rs.845 to about Rs.700-750 each. The pricing lever cannot fix this: a price cut to the comparables' band pushes COGS to 60.4% on the f-tier, which is the arithmetic coupling trap - cost price does not move with the denominator - and a COGS action with no rupee-denominated reference would manufacture a supplier negotiation out of our own price move. A 10-15% cost improvement is a plausible conversation and is the highest-value margin lever available to this account. Five video creatives were generated for this run, one per product, each with its own handle, so no product's ad is blocked on another's render., Ask seller to confirm launch AOV band, then set a 2x/3x coupon ladder. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to confirm the launch AOV band once the first orders land, then set a generic bumper coupon at about 2x that AOV and a generic retention coupon at about 3x that AOV — do not set the bands before the first complete week Reasoning: get_seller_website_checkout_config confirms active_generic_coupon_count is 0 and aov_for_coupon_check is null — the account has no coupon ladder and, being pre-live with zero orders, no AOV to size one against. Set payment modes to online + partial-COD and default to online. |DETAILS| Instruction: Set storefront payment modes to ['online', 'partial-cod'] and default the first entry to 'online' (so the storefront default is online, not partial-COD). Flipping to ['online', 'partial-cod'] with first entry 'online' is the smallest deterministic move that drops plain COD and reinforces the new mix. Razorpay is integrated (is_razorpay: true), so 'online' is wired. Partial-COD is the seller-confirmed precondition from item 1; do not run this action until that is done. The flip must run together with the push flag in the next action because flipping modes without the push flag leaves buyers defaulting to the first entry silently., Set push_for_online_payments = true on the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller / growth lead to turn push_for_online_payments = true on memoriescraft.in, in lockstep with the payment-mode flip. There is no automated action_type for this flag in the catalogue — emit it as a manual seller / growth-lead task with no action_type, per the rule that any storefront change with no automation goes out as a manual action with the specifics in instruction_text. Must land together with the payment_mode update above., Sweep storefront creatives for 'Rs 359' / 'flat Rs 359' claims before the price update. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to confirm no live storefront creative (homepage banner, A+ widget, sticky ribbon, category-page header, badge) leads with 'Rs 359' or 'flat Rs 359'. Reasoning: Bet A, item 3 (creative sweep). Repricing without a creative sweep creates a checkout-time lie: the creative says Rs 359, the storefront says Rs 349, the buyer sees them diverge. Listing it as a manual seller-consent task because storefront creative edits require the seller's sign-off. Same precondition as item 8 in strategy f86d7d14 — emitted once under each parent strategy so each strategy has its own watch., Confirm partial-COD is operationally wired (gateway + courier + warehouse) before flipping payment modes. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to confirm three operational conditions before we restrict payment modes away from plain COD: (a) Razorpay supports the partial-payment-COD flow and the partial-cod gateway flag is set; (b) the courier on the launch set accepts partial-COD collection on delivery; (c) warehouse dispatch flow can handle the dual-charging/prepaid remainder. Customised-products catalogue cannot run plain COD per Branch A of the customised-payment-modes policy (hygiene sweep explicitly flags action_id RESTRICT_TO_ONLINE_AND_PARTIAL_COD). Operational confirmation needed because partial-COD cuts across gateway config, courier routing, and warehouse flow — none of which are visible to a campaign-level tool. Razorpay is integrated (is_razorpay: true) so the online path is wired; partial-COD needs the seller to confirm before flipping the storefront mode. Without this, the payment-mode flip produces a broken checkout.

Enable online payment on the storefront (Razorpay). |DETAILS| Instruction: Three coordinated edits on get_seller_website_checkout_config: (a) integrate Razorpay (preferred — UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets) so is_razorpay=true, (b) add "online" to settings_payment_mode so the list reads "cod, online" (or "online, cod"), and (c) set push_for_online_payments=true. Then run a ₹1 test transaction end-to-end to confirm the gateway is live. Do NOT mark complete until the seller has confirmed in writing that the test transaction cleared and the Razorpay dashboard shows a settled payment. COD must remain enabled and functional throughout — the tripwire is "does enabling online payment break the COD path", and the launch is conditional on COD still working for buyers who choose it. This action MUST land before any paid Meta campaign begins; without it the storefront is COD-only and 25–35% settled RTO is the realistic floor, which makes any ad spend unprofitable from day 1. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) confirms settings_payment_mode="cod", is_razorpay=is_paytm=is_easebuzz=false, push_for_online_payments=false. Hygiene sweep flagged this as HIGH. The launch thesis (a paid Meta campaign on this catalogue) is unworkable on a COD-only storefront because the assortment (apparel, jewellery, accessories) sits in a high-COD, high-RTO category, and the literature on this platform says COD-only stores have a 25–35% settled RTO floor. The tripwire is "did enabling online payment break COD" — online payment has to be added, not replace COD, and the gateway has to be integration-tested, not just toggled., Resolve the expired / null custom domain. |DETAILS| Instruction: Two paths. (a) If the seller has a custom domain: renew it at the registrar, point it at the Shopdeck storefront, and confirm the SSL certificate is valid. (b) If the seller does not have a custom domain: confirm in writing that the default Shopdeck storefront URL is the live storefront and the "expired" flag on custom_domain is a stale signal rather than a real outage. Do NOT mark complete until (a) the storefront URL responds with HTTP 200, and (b) if a custom domain is in use, the SSL certificate validates. This action must land before any paid Meta campaign begins — paid traffic landing on a 404 / failed-SSL storefront burns budget with zero conversion. The seller should set a calendar reminder at day 25 from completion to re-verify the domain is not approaching expiry again. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows custom_domain=null. The hygiene sweep flagged this as MED, the strategy stage escalated it to a launch-blocker because paid Meta traffic on a 404 storefront is a 100% budget loss with zero chance of recovery. The verification step (HTTP 200 + valid SSL) is in the instruction, not the metric, because it is a one-time check, not a continuously-watched number. The day-25 reminder belongs in the operator's calendar, not in the action., Set up the first coupon ladder (2 bands at 2x-AOV and 3x-AOV). |DETAILS| Instruction: Create two generic coupons. (1) 2x-AOV band: coupon_code="WELCOME2X", coupon_title="Welcome 2x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=1500, coupon_max_discount_amount=200, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. (2) 3x-AOV band: coupon_code="WELCOME3X", coupon_title="Welcome 3x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=2400, coupon_max_discount_amount=400, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. aov_for_coupon_check is null (no order history), so the bands use the strategy stage's catalogue-derived estimate: AOV ~₹600–800 across the 7 hero SKUs post-reprice, so 2x ≈ ₹1,500 and 3x ≈ ₹2,400. Confirm bands and discount levels with the seller before publishing — keep discounts at 5–10%, not 15%+, so the coupon does not eat margin. The two coupons together count as one ladder; do NOT exceed 2 active generic coupons at this stage. This action is non-blocking for the launch campaign (the launch can run without coupons), but should land before paid traffic begins so a first-time buyer has a lever to convert. The payload below carries band 1 (WELCOME2X); band 2 (WELCOME3X) is the separate action that follows. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows active_generic_coupon_count=0, active_generic_coupons=null, aov_for_coupon_check=null. Hygiene sweep and strategy stage both flagged this. With no order history, AOV is unmeasurable, so the bands use the catalogue-derived estimate (₹600–800 across the 7 hero SKUs post-reprice): 2x = ₹1,500, 3x = ₹2,400. The 5–10% discount cap is a margin protection — Shopdeck sellers who run 15%+ coupon discounts on pre-launch products typically see coupon conversion eat the entire marketing margin. The expiry date is 6 months out (2027-04-14) so the coupons do not have to be touched again in this run., Set up the 3x-AOV coupon band. |DETAILS| Instruction: Create the second generic coupon. coupon_code="WELCOME3X", coupon_title="Welcome 3x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=2400, coupon_max_discount_amount=400, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. Reasoning: Same logic as the 2x band: catalogue-derived AOV estimate ₹600–800, 3x = ₹2,400. The pair together form the 2-band ladder the strategy stage required. Issued as a separate action rather than merged with the 2x band so each band can be confirmed and verified independently — a failed create on the 3x band should not roll back a confirmed 2x band., Install and verify the Meta pixel on the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: Three steps. (1) Install the Meta pixel on the storefront (via the Shopdeck pixel/marketing-settings integration — not a manual code edit). (2) Verify in Events Manager that the pixel fires on the four key events: ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase. Use a test purchase to confirm the Purchase event lands with the right conversion value. (3) Confirm only ONE pixel id is installed (the catalogue-quality summary reported products_with_multiple_pixel_ids=0, so the starting state is clean — keep it that way). This action MUST land before any paid Meta campaign begins: the lookalike seed for week 4+ is built from the pixel's purchase events, and without the pixel the campaign runs on broad-interest targeting with no purchase signal to optimise against for the entire first 30 days. The tripwire is "pixel double-fires" — verify the Events Manager event volume matches the actual test purchase count. Reasoning: Catalogue-quality summary shows products_with_multiple_pixel_ids=0 (clean starting state) and the diagnosis established that the account has zero pixel events on record. Hygiene sweep did not flag a pixel issue (because there is no pixel to flag), but the diagnosis correctly identified that without a verified pixel the launch campaign has no signal. The strategy stage escalated this to a launch-blocker in item 6 of the work order. The instruction explicitly names all four events and a test-purchase verification, because the most common failure mode is installing a pixel that fires on PageView but not on Purchase., Add Facebook and Instagram social links to the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: In the storefront settings, set facebook_url to the seller's active Facebook page URL and instagram_url to the seller's active Instagram profile URL. Confirm both URLs are correct and point at pages the seller actively controls — not placeholder accounts, not personal profiles, and not the wrong brand. The action is non-blocking (the launch can run without social links) but the strategy stage placed it in the launch-blocker bundle as a small parallel fix. The placeholder-account tripwire is the commonest failure here — a seller copy-pastes the wrong URL or a test page they set up months ago., Bulk-clean the 47,083 placeholder SKUs from the catalogue. |DETAILS| Instruction: PREFERRED PATH — bulk-soft-delete the placeholder SKUs in the catalogue admin. The 17 real product IDs are spelled out so the operator can build the backup before the delete and so the SKU-prefix exclusion has a clean allowlist., Fill the 7 hero product cards (descriptions + 2+ images). |DETAILS| Instruction: For each of the 7 hero SKUs (mgP13ugi, Qk4jaYWA, Sk2awLUS, 9fjacPG2, EkiFC66Z, hVyUvamU, -smoLbl_), add: (a) a 200+ character product description covering fabric, fit, occasion, care, sizing, and what is included in the pack; (b) 2+ product images per SKU (run get_product_images against each short_id to confirm current image counts and fill gaps).
